title: [Core] add and implement `VLLM_LOGITS_PROCESSOR_THREADS` (#12368)

experiments.name: logits_processor_threadpool
experiments.workload: Author's internal custom logits processor on GPU serving, request concurrency ~50, VLLM_LOGITS_PROCESSOR_THREADS=50; end-to-end tok/s and req/s with vs without the threadpool.
experiments.note: Diff adds env var VLLM_LOGITS_PROCESSOR_THREADS (envs.py) and a ThreadPoolExecutor in logits_processor.py that fans the per-sequence logits-processor calls across threads. Number is the author's qualitative '~10% improvement in tok/s and req/s'; author explicitly could not share raw numbers or traces.

reported.scope: end-to-end GPU serving tok/s & req/s with a proprietary custom logits processor at concurrency ~50 and threadpool size 50 (author's internal workload, no in-tree LP shown to benefit)
reported.scale_short: Author's 10% is whole-run E2E with a private logits processor we cannot run; the feature is also off by default and no in-tree LP (e.g. xgrammar) was shown to benefit. TO MAKE 1:1: stand up GPU serving with a CUDA-launching or GIL-releasing custom LP at concurrency 50, set VLLM_LOGITS_PROCESSOR_THREADS=50, and compare steady-state tok/s on vs off.
reported.scale_note: The gain requires a logits processor that either launches extra CUDA kernels or does CPU-bound work while releasing the GIL; the author even added a CUDA sync so threaded LPs don't block each other on the cudaMemcpy lock. With no benefiting in-tree processor and only a published percentage, there is no isolated micro-op to time and no absolute baseline to anchor.

reported.note: author gave a ratio/percentage only; applied to our reproduced baseline
